en: to be heavy-eyed; to be dull; to be drowsy

examples.en: I'm so sleepy that my eyes keep going heavy.

examples.ko: 동생이 잠에서 막 깨서 눈이 게슴츠레해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling just woke up, and their eyes are half-closed and dull.
He looked at me with his eyes half open.
Your eyes look heavy, as if you stayed up all night.

examples.ko: 고양이가 게슴츠레한 눈으로 창밖을 보고 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is looking out the window with drowsy eyes.

examples.ko: 낮잠에서 깬 아이가 게슴츠레한 얼굴로 걸어 나왔어요.
examples.en: The child who woke from a nap came out with a drowsy face.

explain: 주로 '눈이' 뒤에 써서 졸리거나 피곤해서 눈이 반쯤 풀린 모습을 나타내요. '눈을 게슴츠레하게 뜨다'처럼 '-게' 형태로도 자주 써요. 눈 모양을 생생하게 보여 주는 말이라 기운 없고 흐릿한 눈빛에 어울려요.

phrases.en: I turned off the alarm with heavy eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the form used to describe a noun that follows.

phrases.en: He yawned with his eyes half open.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'로 바꿔 눈을 뜨는 모습을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Changing to -게 describes how the eyes are opened.

phrases.example: 어제 못 자서 눈이 게슴츠레해 보여요.
phrases.en: You didn't sleep yesterday, so your eyes look heavy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 그렇게 보인다고 말할 때 '-아/어 보이다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -아/어 보이다 to say that it looks that way.

explain_en: It is mostly used after '눈이' to describe eyes that are half-closed and unfocused from sleepiness or tiredness. The '-게' form is also common, as in '눈을 게슴츠레하게 뜨다'. It paints a vivid picture of the eyes, so it suits a dull, listless look.

examples.en: When I'm nervous, my shoulders stiffen and even my neck hurts.
The interview atmosphere was tense, so it was hard to speak.
When the boss came in, the mood in the meeting room turned stiff.

examples.ko: 오래 앉아 있으면 근육이 경직되기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you sit for a long time, your muscles easily get stiff.

examples.ko: 조직 문화가 경직되면 새 아이디어가 나오기 어려워요.
examples.en: When organizational culture becomes rigid, new ideas are hard to come by.

examples.ko: 그의 표정이 순식간에 경직되는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw his expression stiffen in an instant.

explain: 몸의 근육이 굳을 때와, 분위기·생각·조직이 딱딱해져 융통성이 없을 때 모두 써요. '굳다'가 더 일상적이고 '경직되다'는 조금 격식 있으며, 반대말은 '유연하다'예요.

phrases.en: He was sitting with a stiff expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 긴장해서 굳은 얼굴을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used for a tense, frozen face.

phrases.en: Your muscles get stiff if you sit for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 굳어서 움직이기 힘든 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the body becomes stiff and hard to move.

phrases.example: 생각이 경직되지 않게 여러 의견을 들어요.
phrases.en: I listen to many opinions so my thinking doesn't get rigid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 생각이나 태도가 딱딱하지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say thinking or attitude isn't rigid.

explain_en: It is used both for muscles that tighten and for moods, thinking, or organizations that become rigid and inflexible. '굳다' is more everyday while '경직되다' is somewhat formal, and its opposite is '유연하다'.

examples.en: My son shaved his head and now has a buzz cut.

examples.ko: 옛날 사진 속 아버지는 까까머리 중학생이었어요.
examples.en: In the old photo, my father was a buzz-cut middle schooler.
I met friends from my buzz-cut days after a long time.

examples.ko: 군대에 가기 전에 까까머리로 자르고 왔어요.
examples.en: Before going into the army, he came back with a buzz cut.
Because I have a buzz cut, I always wear a hat in winter.
I touched my younger brother's buzz cut, and it felt bristly.

explain: 머리카락을 아주 짧게 깎은 머리를 말하는데, 옛날 남학생의 머리를 떠올리게 하고 친근하거나 귀여운 느낌이 있어요. 요즘 일상에서는 '삭발'이나 '스포츠머리'라고도 해요. 다만 '삭발'은 머리를 완전히 미는 것에 더 가까워요.

phrases.en: Students with buzz cuts gathered on the playground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 남학생의 모습을 떠올리게 하는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, recalling old-style schoolboys.

phrases.example: 군대 가기 전에 머리를 까까머리로 깎았어요.
phrases.en: I cut my hair into a buzz cut before joining the army.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리를 아주 짧게 자른다는 뜻으로 '깎다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means cutting hair very short, used with 깎다.

phrases.en: It's summer, so I got a short sporty haircut.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이고, '까까머리'보다 현대적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common today and sounds more modern than 까까머리.

explain_en: It means hair cut very short, and it brings to mind schoolboys of the past, with a friendly or cute feel. In daily speech people today also say '삭발' or '스포츠머리'. However, '삭발' is closer to shaving the head completely.

examples.en: I followed right behind the rear of the car ahead.
There is an ad on the back of the bus.
The puppy just trails along right behind its owner.
The tail end of the train got farther and farther away.

examples.ko: 저는 줄 맨 뒤꽁무니에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I was standing at the very back of the line.
That kid tags along behind his older brother.

explain: '뒤'를 좀 더 생생하고 편하게 말하는 구어체예요. 차나 줄의 맨 끝에도 쓰고, 사람에게 '뒤꽁무니를 쫓아다니다'라고 하면 계속 졸졸 따라다닌다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The puppy follows its owner around everywhere.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가를 계속 졸졸 따라다닌다는 구어체 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A colloquial phrase for tagging along behind someone all the time.

phrases.en: I was standing at the very end of the line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄이나 행렬의 가장 끝을 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say the very end of a line or procession.

phrases.example: 버스 뒷부분에 큰 광고가 붙어 있어요.
phrases.en: A big advertisement is stuck on the back of the bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒤꽁무니'보다 중립적이고 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More neutral and formal than 뒤꽁무니.

explain_en: It is a more vivid, casual way of saying '뒤' (back). It is used for the very end of a car or a line, and '뒤꽁무니를 쫓아다니다' for a person means tagging along behind someone all the time.

examples.en: The child started to cry, twisting his body.
He writhed because his stomach hurt.
I twisted the wire this way and that to make a shape.

examples.ko: 동생이 지루한지 의자에서 몸을 뒤틀고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is squirming in the chair, probably out of boredom.

examples.ko: 사진을 찍을 때 허리를 너무 뒤틀지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't twist your waist too much when taking a photo.

examples.ko: 물고기가 그물 안에서 몸을 뒤틀며 버둥거렸어요.
examples.en: The fish thrashed about in the net, twisting its body.

explain: '비틀다'와 비슷하지만 몸을 심하게 꼬거나 모양이 틀어지게 하는 느낌이 더 강해요. '나무가 뒤틀리다', '심사가 뒤틀리다'처럼 피동형 '뒤틀리다'로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The wooden door warped because of the humidity.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒤틀다'의 피동형으로, 모양이 저절로 틀어진 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form of 뒤틀다, describing something that has twisted out of shape.

phrases.en: The child is sleepy and is crying, squirming around.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아프거나 짜증이 나서 몸을 이리저리 꼬는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows someone twisting their body around because of pain or irritation.

phrases.en: I think I ate spoiled food, and my stomach is churning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배 속이 꼬이듯이 아프거나 불편할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when your stomach feels twisted, painful, or upset.

explain_en: It is similar to '비틀다' but feels stronger, as in twisting the body hard or bending something out of shape. The passive form '뒤틀리다' is also common, as in '나무가 뒤틀리다' (wood warps) and '심사가 뒤틀리다' (to feel sour).

examples.ko: 어릴 때 저는 키만 크고 말라깽이였어요.
examples.en: As a kid I was tall but a real beanpole.
My friend has become really skinny lately.
No matter how much my brother eats, he stays skinny.
Please don't tease me by calling me a skinny stick.
After I started working out, I got away from my skinny build.

examples.ko: 그 말라깽이 아이가 밥을 세 그릇이나 먹었어요.
examples.en: That skinny kid ate three bowls of rice.

explain: 몹시 마른 사람을 조금 놀리듯 또는 친근하게 부르는 말이라, 상대에게 직접 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요. 그냥 말할 때는 '마른 사람'이라고 하고, 비슷한 표현으로 '빼빼'가 있어요.

phrases.en: I've been busy with work lately, so I've gotten really skinny.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몹시 마른 모습을 나타내는 말이라 '말라깽이'와 가깝지만 사람을 부르는 말은 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to '말라깽이', but it describes the look rather than naming a person.
phrases.en_equiv: to be skinny as a stick

phrases.example: 저는 마른 사람이라서 살이 찌고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I'm a thin person, so I want to gain weight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말라깽이'보다 부드럽고 예의 바른 말이라 누구에게나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, more polite way to say it that can be used about anyone.

phrases.en: My younger brother is just tall and looks like a beanpole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 마른 모습을 친한 사이에서 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used casually between close people to say someone is very skinny.

explain_en: It is a teasing or affectionate word for a very thin person, so saying it directly to someone can be rude. A neutral way is '마른 사람', and '빼빼' is a similar word.

en: to be ruddy; to be flushed; to be rubicund

examples.en: The child's cheeks are flushed, maybe because he was embarrassed.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 코끝이 발그레해졌어요.
examples.en: After being outside on a cold day, the tip of my nose turned rosy.
Her face was flushed, so I worried she might have a fever.
Those rosy cheeks like apples are so cute.

examples.ko: 칭찬을 듣자 그녀의 뺨이 발그레하게 달아올랐어요.
examples.en: When she heard the compliment, her cheeks flushed pink.

examples.ko: 아침에 본 아이의 얼굴이 아직도 발그레했어요.
examples.en: The child's face I saw in the morning was still flushed.

explain: '빨갛다'보다 연하고 은은하게 붉은 느낌이에요. 주로 볼, 얼굴, 코끝처럼 부끄러움이나 추위로 살짝 붉어진 모습에 써요.

phrases.en: Her softly flushed cheeks are cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태예요. 볼과 가장 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifying form before a noun, most often paired with cheeks.

phrases.en: My face turned slightly red from embarrassment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어지다'가 붙어 점점 붉어지는 변화를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -아/어지다, it shows a gradual change toward red.

phrases.en: My cheeks turned rosy in the cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 서서히 번지듯 붉어지는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes color spreading gradually into a rosy tint.

explain_en: It describes a softer, gentler red than '빨갛다'. It is mostly used for cheeks, faces or the tip of the nose turning slightly red from shyness or cold.

en: sweating bit by bit; beading (of sweat)

examples.en: It's hot, so sweat keeps beading on my forehead.

examples.ko: 발표 전에 긴장해서 삐질삐질 땀을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: I was nervous before the presentation and broke out in a sweat.
When the teacher called me, I broke into a cold sweat.

examples.ko: 에어컨이 고장 나서 삐질삐질 땀을 흘리며 일했어요.
examples.en: The air conditioner broke, so I worked sweating away.

examples.ko: 거짓말이 들킬까 봐 삐질삐질 땀이 나더라고요.
examples.en: I was afraid my lie would be found out, and I started sweating.

examples.ko: 매운 음식을 먹었더니 삐질삐질 땀이 나요.
examples.en: I ate spicy food and now I'm sweating.

explain: 땀이 조금씩 계속 배어 나오는 모습이에요. 더울 때뿐 아니라 긴장하거나 당황했을 때도 많이 써요. 땀을 아주 많이 흘릴 때는 '뻘뻘'을 써요.

phrases.en: I was nervous and sweated bit by bit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땀이 조금씩 계속 나는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes sweat that keeps coming out little by little.

phrases.example: 거짓말이 들킬까 봐 식은땀이 삐질삐질 났어요.
phrases.en: I broke out in a cold sweat, afraid my lie would be found out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당황하거나 불안할 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when flustered or anxious.

phrases.en: It's hot, so I'm sweating a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땀을 아주 많이 흘릴 때 써서, 조금씩 나는 '삐질삐질'과 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for heavy sweating, unlike the little-by-little 'ppijilppijil'.

explain_en: It describes sweat seeping out bit by bit. It is used not only when hot but also when nervous or flustered. For heavy sweating, '뻘뻘' is used instead.

en: new clothes for the New Year

examples.en: On New Year's morning, I dressed up neatly in my new holiday clothes.

examples.ko: 어머니가 동생에게 줄 설빔을 사 오셨어요.
examples.en: My mother bought new holiday clothes for my younger sibling.
In the old days, people wore a new hanbok as their New Year clothes.
I wore my new holiday clothes and bowed to the elders.
Thanks to the new clothes, it felt like Seollal.

examples.ko: 할머니가 손수 지어 주신 설빔이 아직 있어요.
examples.en: I still have the New Year clothes my grandmother made by hand.

explain: 설날에 새로 입으려고 마련한 옷을 말해요. 요즘은 한복 대신 새 옷을 사 입는 것도 설빔이라고 할 수 있고, 추석에 입는 옷은 '추석빔'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The children wore their New Year clothes and bowed to the elders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설날에 입은 새 옷을 말할 때 가장 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most natural way to talk about new clothes worn on New Year's Day.

phrases.en: I got new clothes for the whole family before the holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마련하다'는 미리 준비하거나 산다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 마련하다 means preparing or buying ahead of time.
phrases.en_equiv: to get New Year clothes ready

phrases.en: I bought a new hanbok as Chuseok clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설에 입는 옷은 '설빔', 추석에 입는 옷은 '추석빔'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Clothes for Seollal are 설빔, and clothes for Chuseok are 추석빔.

explain_en: It is the new clothes prepared to wear on Seollal. Today even a new store-bought outfit can be called 설빔 instead of a hanbok, and clothes worn for Chuseok are called '추석빔'.

examples.ko: 시간이 지나니 흥분이 수그러진 것 같아요.
examples.en: As time passed, the excitement seems to have settled.
His fervor is gradually fading.

examples.ko: 비가 그치니 바람도 수그러지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Now that the rain stopped, the wind seems to be dying down too.
When I got praised, my head bowed on its own.
His voice faded and soon it went quiet.
Let's talk again when your anger has cooled down.

explain: '수그리다'의 피동 느낌으로, 고개가 숙여지거나 기세·화·흥분이 약해질 때 써요. 기세가 약해지는 뜻은 '수그러들다'와 거의 비슷해요.

phrases.en: I was so embarrassed that my head bowed by itself.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저절로' 숙여지는 느낌이라 내 뜻과 상관없이 숙여질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like it happens by itself, without intending to.

phrases.en: The cheering excitement has died down a bit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨겁던 분위기가 약해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a heated mood weakens.

phrases.en: The fever has gone down a bit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족에게는 반말 '수그러졌어'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the casual 수그러졌어 with friends or family.

explain_en: It works like a passive of '수그리다': a head gets lowered, or momentum, anger or excitement weakens. In the sense of weakening, it is very close to '수그러들다'.

en: to be nauseating; to be disgusting; to be repulsive

examples.ko: 생선 비린내가 너무 역해서 못 먹겠어요.
examples.en: The fishy smell is so nauseating that I can't eat it.
A foul smell is coming up from the drain.

examples.ko: 속이 안 좋을 때는 기름진 냄새가 더 역하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: When my stomach is upset, greasy smells feel more nauseating.

examples.ko: 이 약은 맛이 역하지만 몸에는 좋아요.
examples.en: This medicine tastes awful, but it's good for you.

examples.ko: 처음 맡아 본 냄새라서 정말 역했어요.
examples.en: It was a smell I'd never encountered, and it was really revolting.
Which smells people find revolting differs from person to person.

explain: 냄새, 맛, 광경처럼 속이 메슥거리고 거부감이 들 때 써요. '냄새가 역하다'가 가장 자연스러워요. '역겹다'와 비슷하고, 몸이 메슥거리는 상태를 직접 말할 때는 '메스껍다'를 써요.

phrases.en: A nauseating smell is coming from the trash can.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing, modifying a noun.

phrases.en: That taste feels disgusting to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받아들이는 사람의 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses how it feels to the person.

phrases.en: This smell is truly disgusting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 사람의 행동이나 마음에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but can also describe a person's behavior or attitude.

explain_en: It is used for smells, tastes and sights that make you queasy and averse. '냄새가 역하다' is the most natural combination. It is close to '역겹다', and to describe the feeling of nausea itself you say '메스껍다'.

examples.ko: 오래 누워 계시면 욕창이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If a person stays lying down for a long time, bedsores can form.

examples.ko: 간호사가 자세를 자주 바꿔 줘서 욕창을 막아요.
examples.en: Nurses prevent bedsores by changing the patient's position often.

examples.ko: 할머니 등에 욕창 자국이 생겨서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: Grandmother got a pressure sore mark on her back, so we went to the hospital.
Try using an anti-bedsore mattress.
Bedsores are easier to treat if found early.

examples.ko: 침대에만 계신 아버지의 욕창 때문에 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried about my father's bedsores since he stays in bed all the time.

explain: 병원, 간호, 가족 돌봄 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 오래 누워 있거나 앉아 있는 사람에게 생기는 문제라 '욕창이 생기다', '욕창을 예방하다', '욕창 방지'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I laid an anti-bedsore mat on the bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 욕창을 막기 위한 물건이나 방법 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before items or methods meant to prevent bedsores.

phrases.example: 치료를 늦추면 욕창이 심해질 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you delay treatment, the bedsore can get worse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상태가 나빠질 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the condition worsens.

phrases.en: Get bedsore treatment at a hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 간호 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used in talk about hospitals and nursing care.

explain_en: It comes up often in talk about hospitals, nursing and caring for family. Because it affects people who lie or sit for long periods, you will hear '욕창이 생기다', '욕창을 예방하다' and '욕창 방지'.

en: to be toxic; to be poisonous; to be venomous

examples.ko: 이 버섯은 유독해서 먹으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: This mushroom is poisonous, so you must not eat it.
Toxic gas leaked out of the factory.

examples.ko: 유독한 물질은 아이들 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 두세요.
examples.en: Keep toxic substances out of children's reach.
They say the leaves of this plant are poisonous.

examples.ko: 창문을 열어서 유독한 연기가 나가게 했어요.
examples.en: I opened the window to let the toxic smoke out.
In the lab, we used only non-toxic chemicals.

explain: 유독하다는 화학 물질, 가스, 버섯, 식물이 사람에게 해로울 때 써요. 부사 '유독'(특히)과 소리가 같으니 문장에서 구별하세요. 말할 때는 '독성이 있다'가 더 자주 들려요. 반대는 '무독하다'예요.

phrases.example: 이 식물은 독성이 있으니까 만지지 마세요.
phrases.en: This plant is toxic, so don't touch it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유독하다'와 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 유독하다 and more often heard in speech.

phrases.example: 유독한 가스 때문에 창문을 모두 열었어요.
phrases.en: We opened all the windows because of the toxic gas.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유독하다'를 명사 앞에 붙이는 활용형이에요. 가스, 물질과 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun, often used with gas and substances.

phrases.en: This material isn't toxic, so it's safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 해롭지 않다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning it is not harmful.

explain_en: 유독하다 is used when a chemical, gas, mushroom or plant is harmful to people. It sounds like the adverb 유독 (especially), so tell them apart in the sentence. In speech 독성이 있다 is heard more often. The opposite is 무독하다.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 조산 위험이 있으니 쉬라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said there is a risk of premature birth, so I should rest.

examples.ko: 언니는 아기를 조산으로 낳아서 한동안 병원에 있었어요.
examples.en: My sister had her baby prematurely, so she stayed in the hospital for a while.

examples.ko: 조산아로 태어난 동생은 지금 아주 건강해요.
examples.en: My younger brother was born premature, but he is very healthy now.

examples.ko: 스트레스가 조산의 원인이 될 수도 있대요.
examples.en: I heard stress can also be a cause of premature birth.

examples.ko: 조산이었는데도 아기가 잘 자라 줘서 다행이에요.
examples.en: Even though it was a premature birth, the baby grew well, which is a relief.

examples.ko: 임산부는 조산을 막으려고 정기 검진을 꼭 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Pregnant women should get regular checkups to prevent premature birth.

explain: '유산'과 달리 아기가 살아서 태어나요. 조산으로 태어난 아기는 '조산아'나 '미숙아'라고 불러요. '조산원'의 '조산'은 한자가 다른 말(助産)이에요.

phrases.en: Premature babies need special care.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조산으로 태어난 아기를 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a baby born prematurely.

phrases.en: My sister gave birth prematurely at seven months of pregnancy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조산을 동사로 쓴 말이에요. 아기를 낳는 사람이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 조산; the person giving birth is the subject.

phrases.en: If you have a lot of stress, the risk of premature birth goes up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 건강 이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase that often appears in medical and health talk.

explain_en: Unlike '유산' (miscarriage), the baby is born alive. A baby born this way is called a '조산아' or '미숙아'. The '조산' in '조산원' is a different word written with different Chinese characters (助産).

examples.en: She spends a lot of time on grooming.
I decorated the room with flowers, and the mood got brighter.
You're pretty enough even without flashy decoration.

examples.ko: 아이는 엄마 구두를 신고 치장하는 놀이를 좋아해요.
examples.en: The child loves playing dress-up in her mom's shoes.
On the morning of the wedding I was busy getting dolled up.
I want to be recognized for my ability rather than my looks.

explain: 사람의 외모나 방, 건물을 예쁘게 꾸미는 것에 써요. 일상에서는 '꾸미다'가 더 흔하고, 치장은 장식을 더하는 느낌이 있어서 조금 요란하거나 지나치다는 뉘앙스로도 나와요. 보통 '치장하다' 꼴로 써요.

phrases.en: The children decorated the classroom with balloons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '치장'을 동사로 쓴 꼴로, 가장 자주 보는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 치장, which is how you will see it most often.

phrases.en: You're pretty enough even without flashy decoration.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치장이 지나치게 화려하다는 뉘앙스를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries the nuance that the decoration is overdone.

phrases.example: 그는 옷 치장에 신경을 많이 써요.
phrases.en: He pays a lot of attention to dressing up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외모를 꾸미는 일에 마음을 쓴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means putting effort and care into fixing up one's appearance.

explain_en: It is used for making a person's appearance, a room or a building look nice. In daily talk '꾸미다' is more common, and 치장 feels like adding decorations, sometimes with a nuance of being flashy or excessive. It is usually used as '치장하다'.
